details: Bitcoin has seen a nearly 4% decline this October, trading around $81,497 as of October 17, reversing the historical "Uptober" trend. This downturn is attributed to factors like $974 million in forced liquidations, a 3.7% year-over-year CPI inflation rate, and nearly $1 billion in Bitcoin ETF outflows. Other major altcoins like XRP, Solana, and Ethereum have experienced even larger drops of over 10% since October 1.
title: Bitcoin's "Uptober" Reversal: Price Dips Amid Macro Factors

details: Ethereum's price has fallen over 10% this October, currently around $2,428, underperforming Bitcoin. Despite the price decline and $306 million in U.S. spot Ether ETF outflows, 59% of social media posts about ETH remain optimistic. Analytics firm Santiment warns this sustained crowd optimism during a downturn could indicate that panic sellers have not yet exited the market, potentially leading to further declines.
title: Ethereum Underperforms in October, Yet Social Sentiment Remains Bullish

details: As of October 16, the total value locked (TVL) in DeFi, including lending protocols, decreased by $1.34 billion week-over-week, reaching $122.25 billion. During the same period, the stablecoin supply also saw a $1.35 billion reduction, falling to $305.24 billion. Analysts suggest that the similar magnitude of these declines may indicate a broader exit of capital from on-chain markets.
title: DeFi TVL and Stablecoin Supply Witness Significant Weekly Declines

details: Babylon Labs has proposed allowing the decentralized lending protocol Aave to accept native Bitcoin as collateral. This proposal would eliminate the need for custodians or wrapped versions of Bitcoin, potentially enabling BTC holders to borrow stablecoins directly against their assets. This move could encourage Bitcoin holders to retain their assets while accessing liquidity.
title: Aave Considers Accepting Native Bitcoin as Collateral

details: Deepsigma, a decentralized perpetual futures exchange, has unveiled a live paper-trading platform that extends to 77 traditional financial markets, including U.S. equities, indexes, commodities, and Treasury yields. Developed by alumni from major financial and tech firms, the platform aims to bridge traditional finance and on-chain markets by tracking prices through external data feeds without tokenizing or taking custody of underlying assets.
title: Wall Street Veterans Launch DeFi Platform for 77 TradFi Markets

details: Deutsche Bank is reportedly preparing to launch its cryptocurrency custody service, with Bitcoin and Ethereum being the first assets supported. The German rollout is expected within weeks, with plans for expansion into Asian financial centers in 2027. This initiative is part of the bank's broader strategy, which includes stablecoin transactions, tokenized deposits, and blockchain-based securities.
title: Deutsche Bank Outlines Bitcoin & Ethereum Custody Timetable

details: Celestia's native token, TIA, has surged approximately 23% in the last 24 hours and 83% over the past four weeks, significantly outperforming Bitcoin and Ethereum, which have seen declines over the shorter term. Despite the price rally, there hasn't been a corresponding increase in data posted to Celestia's network, although daily dollar-valued transaction fees have risen.
title: Celestia's TIA Token Surges While Bitcoin and Ethereum Decline

details: Bloomberg Intelligence strategist Mike McGlone has reiterated a $10,000 target for Bitcoin, suggesting a potential reversion if U.S. stocks experience a 20% drawdown. However, Ki Young Ju, CEO of CryptoQuant, counters this view, arguing that Bitcoin's on-chain floor is closer to $30,000, citing $58 billion in ETF inflows and 1.3 million treasury BTC holdings.
title: Bloomberg Predicts $10K Bitcoin, CryptoQuant CEO Disagrees
